speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your new movement symptoms, could you describe what they feel like and when they started? Also, have you recently started taking any new psychiatric medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you experiencing any involuntary muscle spasms, such as your neck twisting or your eyes rolling upward? If so, do these movements feel painful or uncomfortable?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: This sounds like akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotics like risperidone. I would like to formally check your motor function; REQUEST TEST: Neurological_Exam.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Neurological examination shows mental status alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation with improved psychotic symptoms. Cranial nerves are intact. Motor examination reveals normal tone and strength in all extremities with no involuntary movements noted. Sensory examination is intact. Coordination is normal. Gait is normal, but the patient exhibits an inability to sit still with frequent pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your symptoms and the exam findings, this is consistent with akathisia, a side effect of risperidone characterized by inner restlessness. I will adjust your medication regimen to address this discomfort. DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia
